I have been farming these 6 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I know every patch of soil. At 74, my legs are not what they used to be, but my eyes and my memory are still sharp. My household has five people — my son and daughter-in-law work part-time at a factory in the county town, so they are not always around during busy seasons. My grandson is in school. That means most of the day-to-day field work falls on me and my wife. I cannot afford to take risks or try fancy new methods. I do what has worked before.

This year, I will keep 3.5 mu in cotton and 2.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, same as last year. Cotton is my main cash crop, but it is labor-intensive, so I cannot manage more than that with my age and limited family labor. The wheat is already in the ground from last October. It is April now, and the wheat is at jointing stage. I will topdress it with about 10 kg of urea per mu and irrigate once in early spring. I will harvest it in early June, and immediately after harvest I will plant summer maize. There is no time to plough — I will hire my neighbor's no-tillage planter for the maize, just like everyone else in the village does. For the cotton, I will rotary till the 3.5 mu in mid-to-late April because cotton needs loose soil for the taproot. I will plant an improved variety — probably guoxinmian or something similar from the seed dealer — and put down compound fertilizer as basal dressing. Cotton needs a lot of pesticide; the bollworms never sleep, so I will spray about 13 times from June through August. I will irrigate the cotton twice, once at flowering and once at boll-setting, because pumping from the well is expensive and I must be careful with water. For maize, I will buy hybrid seed — denghai605 is what most people use here — apply compound fertilizer at sowing, and maybe one urea topdressing at the big trumpet leaf stage. Maize only needs two pesticide sprays and one or two irrigations. I apply a bit more fertilizer than the extension agent recommends because a few years ago I tried cutting back and the yield dropped, and at my age I cannot afford a bad year. I would rather spend a little more on inputs than risk losing half my harvest.
